title: Filestage vs Gigxomi for Video Review and Agency Delivery
excerpt: Compare Filestage's structured file review and approval workflows with Gigxomi's broader video editing agency operations.
seoDescription: Filestage vs Gigxomi for video editing agencies: compare structured file review and approvals with client, editor, delivery, and payout operations.
featuredImageAlt: Filestage versus Gigxomi video review and delivery comparison
introduction: Filestage concentrates on structured review and approval across videos and other file types, including reviewer groups, versions, comments, and decisions. Gigxomi concentrates on the editing agency around the file: customer conversations, managers, editors, assignments, review, delivery, accounting, and payouts. The products overlap at review but differ substantially in scope.
verdict: Choose Filestage when formal multi-stage approval, external reviewer groups, support for varied creative file types, and proofing governance drive the purchase. Choose Gigxomi when the agency needs a connected operating system and review is one stage among sales, production, and finance. Teams can combine them by keeping authoritative file decisions in Filestage and authoritative work ownership in Gigxomi.

sections.heading: Filestage's strongest use case
paragraphs: Complex client work may require several groups to approve in sequence: an internal creative lead, the client marketing team, legal, and a final brand owner. Filestage provides a structured environment for those reviewers to see the relevant version, add contextual feedback, and make a recorded decision.

The ability to review more than video is important for campaigns that include thumbnails, scripts, PDFs, social graphics, and other collateral. One proofing discipline can cover the complete package even when the production work spans several specialist teams.
bullets: Proofing across varied creative file types

sections.heading: Gigxomi covers a different source of delay
paragraphs: Some agencies do not lose time inside review; they lose time before and after it. Customer details sit in messaging apps, production ownership sits in a task board, the editor asks a manager for missing context, and finance later reconstructs which delivery should create a payout. Better annotations alone do not repair that chain.

Gigxomi is intended to keep those business relationships connected. It is more relevant when the founder wants to delegate the whole service operation, not only improve how a client comments on a file.

sections.heading: Test approval governance, not visual polish
paragraphs: Create a trial with conflicting stakeholders and a real deadline. Configure the correct review order, invite external participants, upload a revision, and ask one reviewer to approve while another requests a change. The system should make the authoritative decision obvious and prevent the team from delivering the wrong version.

Next, trace that decision into agency operations. Who receives the next action? Does the editor know whether work is complete? Can the manager deliver confidently? Does the approved milestone connect to the correct billing or payout state? This cross-boundary test exposes the need for an operating layer.

sections.heading: Migration and coexistence advice
paragraphs: If Filestage remains, document it as the source of truth for review comments, versions, and approvals. Store only the active review link and milestone in Gigxomi. Use consistent client and deliverable identifiers, and prevent feedback from being repeated in chat after reviewers have entered the proofing stage.

If simpler Gigxomi review replaces Filestage, preserve completed approval records according to client and legal requirements. Pilot the most demanding active account before changing contracts or promises. A tool reduction should not remove a control the client expects.

sections.heading: Which buying team should choose each
paragraphs: Filestage fits marketing departments and creative agencies whose hardest problem is coordinating formal feedback across many stakeholders and file formats. Procurement should evaluate reviewer experience, proofing governance, storage, security, and the required plan limits using current official information.

Gigxomi fits video editing businesses seeking operational unity around conversations, assignments, delivery, and money. Use both when the agency sells complex approval as part of its service and also needs to control the complete client-to-editor lifecycle.

decisionChecklist: How many reviewer groups approve a typical deliverable?
Does the campaign include files beyond video?
Which approval record is contractually authoritative?
How does an approved file trigger delivery and financial action?
Can clients use the review experience without creating internal confusion?
What records must be retained if proofing tools change?
